executive_summary: Repository scores 86.0/100 — _strong_foundation_ band. Strongest: #01 Architectural coherence (5/5, weight 15%). Weakest: #05 Test strategy (3/5, weight 10%). Highest-leverage improvement: Run the Vitest suite in CI on PRs and add at least a store persistence/hydration integration test..

rationale: Overall score 86.0 maps to stage=mature_platform per aggregation rules.

evidence.claim: Strict layering: pure domain logic (no reactivity, no I/O) lives in operations.ts, with a header documenting the boundary against the reactive shell.
The reactive shell is a thin wrapper that delegates every mutation to the pure ops module and only adds $state + persistence — separation of concerns is explicit.
Two ADRs pin the load-bearing decisions (storage envelope, deletion rule) as contracts the store, seed, and tests depend on; both Implemented and cross-linked.
Domain layer (lib/) never imports from the routes/ layer — dependency direction points inward.
Domain types are a single hand-written source of truth that components and ops import from; route/page structure mirrors the three entities cleanly.

strengths.point: Testability-driven layering: rules are pure functions over a plain AppData, so they unit-test without a DOM while store.svelte.ts owns reactivity and persistence.
Decisions that impose cross-component contracts are captured as ADRs rather than buried in the diff, with a maintained index.

risks.point: The store singleton is a hard module-level coupling point for every route; acceptable at this size but it is the one global the whole app reaches through.

up_one.condition: Already at ceiling — boundaries, enforced dep direction, ADRs, and clear ownership are all present.

down_one.condition: Move referential-integrity rules out of operations.ts into route handlers, dissolving the pure-domain boundary.

no-lib-imports-from-routes.claim: No file under src/lib imports from src/routes — the domain layer has no upward dependency on the UI layer.

evidence.claim: svelte-check passes with 0 errors, 0 warnings across 4864 files.
ESLint passes clean on the project source with zero findings.
Domain functions are small, single-purpose, and immutable (each returns a new AppData); naming carries intent (canDeleteUser, dashboardStats, periodOf).
Doc comments across the domain layer explain WHY (injected clock for testable 'this period', the both-edges deletion rule per ADR-002) rather than restating the code.
Validation is a clean field-to-message-map pattern reused consistently across user/project/report validators.

strengths.point: Pluralization and human-readable deletion messages are handled carefully and consistently in one place.
Result-object error returns (ok/reason) instead of thrown exceptions make the failure path explicit and locally reasoned.

risks.point: The only `any` usage is two eslint-disabled generic-type helpers in utils.ts (vendored shadcn pattern), bounded and annotated rather than pervasive.

up_one.condition: Already at ceiling — clean naming, intentional abstraction, lint + typecheck enforced and green.

down_one.condition: Introduce significant duplication of the validation field-map logic into route components instead of reusing validation.ts.

evidence.claim: Multi-stage Dockerfile builds and runs the adapter-node artifact with a pinned node:24-alpine base and NODE_ENV=production.
CI runs on every push/PR to dev and main: type-check + build with pinned Node 24 and npm ci against the committed lockfile.
Separate dev/prod deploy workflows push images to GHCR and deploy to EC2, with all secrets injected from GitHub Secrets at runtime (never committed).
README documents install/run/build/test entry points and states no env vars are required for this frontend-only app.
Lint and test are NOT run in CI even though both are configured locally and in the husky pre-commit/lint-staged chain.

strengths.point: Reproducible builds: lockfile committed, Node pinned via engines and .nvmrc, npm ci in CI and Docker.
Deploy is effectively push-button per branch (push to dev/main → image build → EC2 compose up).

risks.point: CI gates on check+build but not lint or the 35-test Vitest suite, so a green PR can still ship lint/test regressions.
No logging/metrics/health endpoint and no env validation at startup — expected for a static client app but limits the operational ceiling.
Deploy infra still injects Supabase env vars (template residue) the frontend-only app never reads; harmless but noise on the prod path.

up_one.condition: Add lint + test (and a health/readiness probe) to CI so the configured quality gates actually run on PRs.

down_one.condition: Remove the CI workflow or the Dockerfile so there is no reproducible build/deploy path.

no-health-endpoint.claim: No HTTP health/readiness endpoint or structured logger exists; the app is a client-rendered SPA (ssr=false) served by adapter-node.

evidence.claim: TypeScript strict is enabled in the primary tsconfig, with checkJs on.
svelte-check passes with zero type errors across the whole project.
Domain unions are const-asserted arrays driving both the type and runtime validation, so the validator and the type stay in lockstep (single source of truth).
Persisted localStorage input — the one true external boundary — is runtime-validated (version + array shape) before being trusted, with a corrupt-payload fallback to re-seed.
Form payload types are derived (Omit) from the entity types so ids/timestamps cannot be supplied by a form, enforced statically.

strengths.point: Runtime validators re-check membership against the const unions (ROLES/STATUSES) so an out-of-band value is rejected, not just statically discouraged.
DeleteResult / DeleteCheck discriminated unions force callers to handle the failure branch.

risks.point: The localStorage shape guard validates only top-level structure (version + arrays), not per-record field types, so a hand-edited but structurally-valid blob could carry malformed records.
No schema library (Zod/Valibot) and no contract tests — appropriate for a no-backend MVP but the gap to a 5 is the lack of generated/contract-tested boundaries.

up_one.condition: Add a schema validator (e.g. Zod) parsing the persisted blob field-by-field at the localStorage boundary, replacing the hand-rolled shape check.

no-schema-library.claim: No runtime schema-validation library (Zod/Valibot/Yup) is a dependency; boundary validation is hand-rolled in validation.ts and the store.

evidence.claim: Vitest suite runs and passes: 35 tests across 4 files, all green.
Operations tests cover CRUD immutability, both referential-integrity rules (block + allow), and the subtle this-period-by-reportingPeriod-not-createdAt edge case.
Seed tests assert the ADR-002 demonstrability contract directly — that the dataset proves the deletion rule both ways.
Validation tests cover happy paths and negative cases including malformed email, invalid period (2026/6 and 2026-13), and missing-reference rejection.
Tests are NOT wired into any CI workflow, so they do not gate PRs.

strengths.point: Tests target the genuinely load-bearing logic (referential integrity, dashboard period semantics, timestamp preservation on edit) — not coverage padding.
Clock is injected into tested code so time-dependent assertions are deterministic.

risks.point: Tests are unit-only over pure functions; the reactive store, persistence round-trip, and Svelte components/routes have zero test coverage.
No CI execution of the suite — a regression that breaks a domain rule would not block a merge.

up_one.condition: Run the Vitest suite in CI on PRs and add at least a store persistence/hydration integration test.

down_one.condition: Delete the operations/validation test files, leaving only trivial coverage.

no-component-or-store-tests.claim: All four test files target pure modules (operations, validation, seed, utils); no test exercises store.svelte.ts, components, or routes.

scalability_extensibility.confidence_reason: Small surface area; extensibility judged from the entity-symmetric module/route structure and the documented scaling assumptions rather than from observed growth.

evidence.claim: Adding a new entity follows a clear, repeatable seam: a type in types.ts, a validator, a set of pure ops, store methods, and a parallel route group — each of the three current entities is structured identically.
Routes are organized per-entity under (app)/ with new/[id]/[id]/edit sub-routes, so entities (and engineers) don't collide.
Scaling assumptions are explicitly ADR'd: single-key whole-blob writes, ~5MB localStorage ceiling, no cross-tab sync — bounded for a single-user internal MVP.
No N+1 / unbounded hot-path footguns: dashboard stats are simple array filters over an in-memory dataset of a few hundred rows.

strengths.point: The version field in the persisted envelope is a deliberate forward-compatibility hook for future schema migration rather than a crash on stale data.
Pure-ops + thin-store split means the persistence layer could be swapped (e.g. to a real backend) by reimplementing the store without touching domain rules.

risks.point: The whole-dataset rewrite on every mutation and the in-memory full-array scans are O(n) and fine only under the documented MVP volume; they are the first thing to hurt if the tool outgrows its bounds.

up_one.condition: Introduce a persistence-adapter interface so the localStorage backend is a swappable plugin point with an ADR'd contract.

down_one.condition: Add a per-row loop that re-reads/re-persists the whole blob inside a render hot path.

evidence.claim: No hardcoded secrets in tracked source, CI, or Docker; all deploy secrets are GitHub Secrets injected at runtime, and .env.example holds placeholders only.
No eval / new Function / innerHTML / dangerous-HTML sinks in application source (UI primitives excluded).
The localStorage trust boundary is defensively handled: parse is wrapped in try/catch and a corrupt or stale payload falls through to a clean re-seed rather than crashing.
All form input flows through validators that reject malformed values and dangling references before any mutation.
Deletion guards fail closed and explain the reason, rather than silently cascading or throwing.

strengths.point: Minimal attack surface by design: frontend-only, no auth, no server-side input handling, ssr disabled — fewer trust boundaries to get wrong.
Secret hygiene is reinforced by a husky pre-commit chain that runs the Dynamo staged-secrets scan.

risks.point: No SAST/dependency-scanning in CI and no threat model document, which is the gap between 4 and 5.

Persisted data is fully client-trusted: a user editing their own localStorage can inject arbitrary record contents (rendered as text, but unvalidated per-field). Low impact for a single-user local tool.

up_one.condition: Add a SAST/dependency-audit workflow to CI and document the (minimal) trust model.

down_one.condition: Introduce a hardcoded secret in tracked source or render persisted data via an HTML sink.

secrets-in-env-only.claim: All secret material is referenced via env vars / GitHub Secrets; .env.example contains placeholders only and no secret pattern is present in tracked source, CI, or Docker.

no-sast-in-ci.claim: No SAST, CodeQL, or dependency-audit step exists in any CI workflow.

evidence.claim: Full doc backbone present and accurate: README (rewritten to match the auth-shell removal), CHANGELOG (Keep-a-Changelog format), two cross-linked ADRs with an index, plus a STYLEGUIDE.md.
Lint + format + type-check are all configured (ESLint flat config, Prettier, svelte-check) and enforced pre-commit via husky + lint-staged.
ADRs document contract-shaping decisions with Context/Options/Decision/Consequences, both marked Implemented, indexed in decisions/README.md.
Conventional-commit history: feat:/chore: subjects, the MVP merged via squash PR (#9), no wip/fix dump commits.
Dependencies are pinned via a committed lockfile and Node is pinned via engines + .nvmrc.

strengths.point: README is a true single onramp — install/run/build/test, layout tree, and a 'How it works' section that points at the ADRs.
Lint-config carries WHY comments explaining the two intentional rule/ignore choices, rather than silent disables.

risks.point: ESLint ignores src/routes/styleguide/ but that route no longer exists — a stale config reference (minor cleanup debt).
CLAUDE.md is .gitignored (line 63) yet committed and tracked, and it is not Prettier-clean — a small standards/hygiene slip.

up_one.condition: Already at ceiling — ADRs, cross-linked docs, enforced lint/format, conventional history, pinned deps.

down_one.condition: Drop the lint/format pre-commit enforcement or let the README drift from the code again.

conventional-commit-style.claim: All commits use conventional-commit subjects (feat:/chore:) with meaningful messages; the MVP landed as a squash-merge PR, no garbage commits.

evidence.claim: Zero TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX markers anywhere in application source (UI primitives excluded).
The debt that exists is template residue and is explicitly declared in the README: the Supabase auth shell was removed and the infra/ dir 'ships with the template and is unused by this app'.
No competing/duplicated patterns: one validation style, one store, one persistence path, one deletion-rule definition (ADR-002).
Clean, conventional recent history with no churn or revert noise.

strengths.point: Brittle assumptions are surfaced as ADR consequences (no cross-tab sync, 5MB ceiling, invariants enforced by code not structure) rather than left implicit.

risks.point: Undeclared residue: package.json still lists @supabase/ssr and @supabase/supabase-js deps and a self-erroring gen:types script the frontend-only app never uses; the README declares the infra residue but not these.
CI build injects unused Supabase stub env vars and the eslint config references a removed styleguide route — small dangling template artifacts.

up_one.condition: Strip the unused Supabase dependencies, gen:types script, CI stub env, and stale eslint ignore so the manifest matches the declared frontend-only scope.

down_one.condition: Introduce untracked TODO/FIXME markers in hot paths or let a second persistence pattern coexist with the store.

clean-recent-history.claim: The full commit history uses meaningful conventional-commit messages with no wip/fix/misc dump commits.
